events.what: Chen and Hou give a rigorous computer-assisted proof of finite-time blowup for 3D axisymmetric Euler with smooth data in a smooth bounded domain (boundary singularity)
events.source: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2210.07191 (Part I, per search result); journal version https://www.pnas.org/doi/10.1073/pnas.2500940122

events.what: DeepMind 'Discovery of Unstable Singularities': PINN numerical discovery of unstable self-similar profiles for Euler-with-boundary, Boussinesq, IPM, CCF; explicitly not a proof

Ganeshram, Duruisseaux, Anandkumar (and companion with George): PINN-found, numerically certified candidate singular profile for unforced Euler on R^3, with stability framework conditional on certifying remaining estimates

judgement.doubts: Chen-Hou's first written argument is the 2022 arXiv preprint series (2210.07191, Part I), not the Jan 2025 PNAS receipt date; a pre-snapshot case result is a note on a still-open problem. If one read the PNAS paper as containing substantially new mathematics beyond the 2022 preprints, status would be partial (direction refuted, i.e. blowup, not 'confirmed'). The Ganeshram et al. work is a reduction to uncertified estimates by the authors' own words, so scope none; if certified it would be a whole-problem claim. The PINN is an AI system producing the candidate profile; if that work ever counts it would be 'generated'/'assisted'. Event object left as recorded (Chen-Hou) for evidence; it no longer sets the status. Forced-Euler (Alpoge-Buckmaster) is a variant.

corrections.why: F7: the record dates Chen-Hou by PNAS receipt (13 Jan 2025), but their proof's first written argument is the 2022 arXiv series (2210.07191), before the snapshot; the only post-snapshot events are numerical discovery (DeepMind 2025) and a conditional framework the authors say is not a complete proof (2609.10867/2609.10860), both scope none. No surviving event; problem not resolved pre-snapshot, so open.
F14: open carries null; moreover Chen-Hou proves blowup, which is not 'confirmed' regularity.
